records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת בְּנֵי־נֹ֔חַ שֵׁ֖ם חָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וַיִּוָּלְד֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם בָּנִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] generations of [the] sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth; and were born to them sons after the flood.
pieces: This is the account of the families of Noah's sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.

L.1: And these [are] the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.

R.1: This is the list of the families that came from Noah's sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth. They had sons after the flood.

decisions.choice: the generations of the sons of Noah: the Table of Nations
alternatives: a family tree of individuals only
decisions.reason: The chapter lists the peoples that came from Noah's three sons. Many names are of peoples, cities or lands rather than single persons ("the Jebusites", "Egypt"), and "fathered" can mean "was the ancestor of". Counted, the names come to about seventy, a number later used for the nations of the world. The list groups peoples by family, language, land and nation (verses 5, 20, 31), not by race or color.

decisions.choice: after the flood: the whole of humankind begins again from Noah
decisions.reason: Every people listed descends from the family saved in the ark (9:19). The chapter fulfils the blessing "fill the earth" (9:1).

records.heading: The families of Noah's sons

records.source: בְּנֵ֣י יֶ֔פֶת גֹּ֣מֶר וּמָג֔וֹג וּמָדַ֖י וְיָוָ֣ן וְתֻבָ֑ל וּמֶ֖שֶׁךְ וְתִירָֽס׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan and Tubal and Meshech and Tiras.
pieces: The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.

L.2: The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.

R.2: Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras.

decisions.choice: Japheth's line: the peoples to the north and west
decisions.reason: Several names are known peoples: Madai is the Medes, Javan the Ionian Greeks, and Gomer, Tubal and Meshech peoples of Asia Minor (Ezekiel 38:2-6). The peoples of Japheth's line lived north and west of Israel, toward Asia Minor and the Mediterranean islands.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י גֹּ֑מֶר אַשְׁכֲּנַ֥ז וְרִיפַ֖ת וְתֹגַרְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz and Riphath and Togarmah.
pieces: The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.

L.3: And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.

R.3: Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י יָוָ֖ן אֱלִישָׁ֣ה וְתַרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּתִּ֖ים וְדֹדָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Javan: Elishah and Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.
pieces: The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittim and the Dodanim.

L.4: And the sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.

R.4: Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim and Dodanim.

decisions.choice: Dodanim, as in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters for d and r look alike. 1 Chronicles 1:7, the Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read Rodanim, the people of Rhodes, which fits a list of Greek and island peoples. The Hebrew text of Genesis is followed.

decisions.choice: Tarshish and Kittim: places across the sea
decisions.reason: Tarshish is a distant port to the west, reached by ship (Jonah 1:3). Kittim is Cyprus, named after its city Kition. Both are seafaring peoples of Javan's (Greek) branch.

records.source: מֵ֠אֵלֶּה נִפְרְד֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ בְּאַרְצֹתָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לִלְשֹׁנ֑וֹ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: From these separated the coastlands of the nations in their lands, each according to its language, according to their clans, in their nations.
pieces: From these the peoples of the coasts and islands spread out into their own lands, each with its own language, by their clans and nations.

L.5: From these the coastland peoples of the nations spread out in their lands, each with its own language, by their clans, in their nations.

R.5: These were the people who spread out to the coasts and islands. They lived in their own lands, in their own families and nations, each with its own language.

decisions.choice: the coastlands of the nations: the peoples of the coasts and islands
decisions.reason: The word means coastlands or islands, the lands along the Mediterranean as seen from Israel (Isaiah 11:11).

decisions.choice: each with its own language: told before the story of Babel
decisions.reason: The chapter already speaks of many languages, though 11:1-9 tells how the languages came to be divided. Genesis groups its material by theme: chapter 10 shows the result, the spreading of the nations, and chapter 11 tells how it began.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י חָ֑ם כּ֥וּשׁ וּמִצְרַ֖יִם וּפ֥וּט וּכְנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Ham: Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan.
pieces: The sons of Ham were Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan.

L.6: And the sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.

R.6: Ham's sons were Cush, Egypt, Put and Canaan.

decisions.choice: Ham's line: the peoples to the south, and Canaan
decisions.reason: Cush is the land south of Egypt (roughly today's Sudan), Mizraim is the usual Hebrew name for Egypt, and Put is probably Libya. Canaan is the land Israel later lived in. Ham's line covers Africa and the lands along the eastern Mediterranean, with an offshoot in Mesopotamia (verses 8-12).

decisions.choice: Egypt
decisions.reason: Mizraim is the Hebrew name of Egypt; Balanced and Readable use the English name. Literal keeps Mizraim.

records.source: וּבְנֵ֣י כ֔וּשׁ סְבָא֙ וַֽחֲוִילָ֔ה וְסַבְתָּ֥ה וְרַעְמָ֖ה וְסַבְתְּכָ֑א וּבְנֵ֥י רַעְמָ֖ה שְׁבָ֥א וּדְדָֽן׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Cush: Seba and Havilah and Sabtah and Raamah and Sabteca. And [the] sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
pieces: The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Dedan.

L.7: And the sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.

R.7: Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah and Sabteca. Raamah's sons were Sheba and Dedan.

decisions.choice: Havilah, Sheba and Dedan: peoples of Arabia
decisions.reason: These are peoples on both sides of the Red Sea, in Arabia and East Africa. Sheba and Havilah also appear in Shem's line (verses 28-29): peoples could be related to more than one family.

records.source: וְכ֖וּשׁ יָלַ֣ד אֶת־נִמְרֹ֑ד ה֣וּא הֵחֵ֔ל לִֽהְי֥וֹת גִּבֹּ֖ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty man on the earth.
pieces: Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became the first great warrior on the earth.

L.8: And Cush fathered Nimrod; he was the first to be a mighty man on the earth.

R.8: Cush was the father of Nimrod. Nimrod became the first great warrior and ruler on earth.

decisions.choice: a mighty man: a warrior, a man of power
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of the "mighty men" of 6:4: a hero or warrior. Nimrod is the first empire-builder named, and "he began" marks him as a first, like the founders in 4:20-22.

decisions.choice: fathered: was the ancestor of
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the chapter, "fathered" may mean a more distant ancestry; Nimrod's kingdom is in Mesopotamia, far from the land of Cush.

records.source: הֽוּא־הָיָ֥ה גִבֹּֽר־צַ֖יִד לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה עַל־כֵּן֙ יֵֽאָמַ֔ר כְּנִמְרֹ֛ד גִּבּ֥וֹר צַ֖יִד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: He was a mighty hunter before YHWH; therefore it is said, like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before YHWH.
pieces: He was a mighty hunter before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; that is why people say, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.9: He was a mighty hunter before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Therefore it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.9: He was a great hunter, known even to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is why people say, "He is like Nimrod, a great hunter before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in the LORD's sight
alternatives: a very great hunter (the LORD's name as a superlative)
decisions.reason: "Before the LORD" usually means in his sight or presence. Here it may simply mark Nimrod's fame ("the greatest hunter there was"); some read it as "against the LORD", in the light of Babel (verse 10; 11:1-9). The saying quoted shows that Nimrod was proverbial.

decisions.choice: known even to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable takes the phrase as fame (m1), and keeps "before the LORD" in the saying.

records.source: וַתְּהִ֨י רֵאשִׁ֤ית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶ֖רֶךְ וְאַכַּ֣ד וְכַלְנֵ֑ה בְּאֶ֖רֶץ שִׁנְעָֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] beginning of his kingdom Babel and Erech and Akkad and Calneh, in [the] land of Shinar.
pieces: His kingdom began with Babylon, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

L.10: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

R.10: His kingdom began with the cities of Babylon, Erech, Akkad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

decisions.choice: Babel, Erech, Akkad, in Shinar: the cities of Babylonia
decisions.reason: Babel is Babylon, Erech is Uruk, and Akkad was a great city of ancient Mesopotamia. Shinar is the Hebrew name for Babylonia, the plain between the Tigris and the Euphrates where the tower is built (11:2).

decisions.choice: Calneh: a city, or "all of them"
alternatives: and all of them were in the land of Shinar
decisions.reason: No city of this name is known in Babylonia. The same letters with different vowels mean "all of them", which would give "and all of them were in the land of Shinar".

decisions.choice: Babylon
decisions.reason: Babel is the Hebrew name of Babylon. Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal keeps Babel, the name of 11:9.

records.source: מִן־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִ֖וא יָצָ֣א אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ אֶת־נִ֣ינְוֵ֔ה וְאֶת־רְחֹבֹ֥ת עִ֖יר וְאֶת־כָּֽלַח׃
records.gloss: From that land he went out to Assyria, and he built Nineveh and Rehoboth-Ir and Calah,
pieces: From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah

L.11: From that land he went out to Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir and Calah,

R.11: From there he went on to Assyria and built the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah

decisions.choice: he went out to Assyria: Nimrod went
alternatives: Asshur went out from that land
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean "he (Nimrod) went out to Asshur" or "Asshur went out". Since the passage is about Nimrod's kingdom, and Micah 5:6 calls Assyria "the land of Nimrod", Nimrod is taken as the subject.

decisions.choice: Nineveh and Calah: great cities of Assyria
decisions.reason: Nineveh, on the Tigris, became Assyria's capital (Jonah 1:2). Calah (Nimrud) was another royal city. Rehoboth-Ir may mean "the city squares", perhaps a part of Nineveh.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־רֶ֔סֶן בֵּ֥ין נִֽינְוֵ֖ה וּבֵ֣ין כָּ֑לַח הִ֖וא הָעִ֥יר הַגְּדֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; that [is] the great city.
pieces: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah; that is the great city.

L.12: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah; that [is] the great city.

R.12: and Resen, which is between Nineveh and Calah. All together these made up the great city.

decisions.choice: that is the great city: Nineveh, or the whole group of cities
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely refers to Nineveh with the cities around it, as Jonah calls Nineveh "the great city" (Jonah 1:2; 3:3).

records.source: וּמִצְרַ֡יִם יָלַ֞ד אֶת־לוּדִ֧ים וְאֶת־עֲנָמִ֛ים וְאֶת־לְהָבִ֖ים וְאֶת־נַפְתֻּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: And Mizraim fathered [the] Ludites and [the] Anamites and [the] Lehabites and [the] Naphtuhites,
pieces: Egypt was the ancestor of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

L.13: And Mizraim fathered the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

R.13: From Egypt came the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,

decisions.choice: names of peoples: plural names ending in -ites
decisions.reason: From here the list names peoples, not persons (the Hebrew ending -im is plural). Mizraim (Egypt) is the ancestor of peoples of North Africa and the Nile.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־פַּתְרֻסִ֞ים וְאֶת־כַּסְלֻחִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֥וּ מִשָּׁ֛ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וְאֶת־כַּפְתֹּרִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: and [the] Pathrusites and [the] Casluhites, from where came out [the] Philistines, and [the] Caphtorites.
pieces: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came) and the Caphtorites.

L.14: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorites.

R.14: the Pathrusites, the Casluhites (the Philistines came from them) and the Caphtorites.

decisions.choice: from whom the Philistines came: their origin
alternatives: the Philistines came from the Caphtorites
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the Philistines are said to have come from Caphtor, probably Crete (Amos 9:7; Jeremiah 47:4). The note may originally have stood after "the Caphtorites", or the two peoples were related.

decisions.choice: Pathrusites: the people of Pathros, Upper Egypt
decisions.reason: Pathros is southern (Upper) Egypt (Isaiah 11:11; Jeremiah 44:1).

records.source: וּכְנַ֗עַן יָלַ֛ד אֶת־צִידֹ֥ן בְּכֹר֖וֹ וְאֶת־חֵֽת׃
records.gloss: And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
pieces: Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of Heth,

L.15: And Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,

R.15: Canaan's oldest son was Sidon. His other sons were Heth

decisions.choice: Sidon and Heth: the Phoenicians and the Hittites
decisions.reason: Sidon is the great Phoenician port city on the coast north of Israel. Heth is the ancestor of the Hittites of Canaan, from whom Abraham buys a burial place (23:3-20).

records.source: וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י וְאֵ֖ת הַגִּרְגָּשִֽׁי׃
records.gloss: and the Jebusite[s] and the Amorite[s] and the Girgashite[s],
pieces: and of the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

L.16: and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

R.16: and the ancestors of the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,

decisions.choice: Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites: the peoples of Canaan
decisions.reason: These are peoples Israel later met in Canaan (15:19-21; Deuteronomy 7:1). The Jebusites held Jerusalem until David took it (2 Samuel 5:6-9).

records.source: וְאֶת־הַֽחִוִּ֥י וְאֶת־הַֽעַרְקִ֖י וְאֶת־הַסִּינִֽי׃
records.gloss: and the Hivite[s] and the Arkite[s] and the Sinite[s],
pieces: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

L.17: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

R.17: the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,

records.source: וְאֶת־הָֽאַרְוָדִ֥י וְאֶת־הַצְּמָרִ֖י וְאֶת־הַֽחֲמָתִ֑י וְאַחַ֣ר נָפֹ֔צוּ מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃
records.gloss: and the Arvadite[s] and the Zemarite[s] and the Hamathite[s]. And afterward were scattered [the] clans of the Canaanite[s].
pieces: the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites. Later the clans of the Canaanites spread out,

L.18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites. Afterward the clans of the Canaanites spread out.

R.18: the Arvadites, the Zemarites and the Hamathites. Later the Canaanite families spread out.

decisions.choice: Arvad, Zemar, Hamath: cities of the north
decisions.reason: These peoples are named after cities of the northern coast and Syria: Arvad, an island city, Zemar, and Hamath on the Orontes river.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֞י גְּב֤וּל הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ מִצִּידֹ֔ן בֹּאֲכָ֥ה גְרָ֖רָה עַד־עַזָּ֑ה בֹּאֲכָ֞ה סְדֹ֧מָה וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאַדְמָ֥ה וּצְבֹיִ֖ם עַד־לָֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: And was [the] border of the Canaanite[s] from Sidon, as you go toward Gerar, as far as Gaza; as you go toward Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
pieces: and the border of Canaan reached from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and then toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

L.19: And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, in the direction of Gerar, as far as Gaza; and in the direction of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

R.19: The land of the Canaanites reached from Sidon in the north, south toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and east toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.

decisions.choice: the border of the Canaanites: the land later promised to Abraham
decisions.reason: The border runs south along the coast from Sidon to Gaza and inland toward the cities of the plain by the Dead Sea (14:2). Lasha is not known. This is roughly the land promised to Abraham (15:18-21).

decisions.choice: as you go toward: in the direction of
decisions.reason: "Your going toward" is a Hebrew way of giving a direction, as a traveler would describe a route.

decisions.choice: in the north; south; east
decisions.reason: Readable adds the compass directions to make the route easier to follow (m1).

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי־חָ֔ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לִלְשֹֽׁנֹתָ֑ם בְּאַרְצֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Ham according to their clans, according to their languages, in their lands, in their nations.
pieces: These are the descendants of Ham, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.

L.20: These [are] the sons of Ham, by their clans and their languages, in their lands and their nations.

R.20: These were Ham's descendants. They lived in their own lands, in their own families and nations, each with its own language.

decisions.choice: by clans, languages, lands, nations: the four ways the peoples are grouped
decisions.reason: Each of the three lists closes with the same four words (verses 5, 20, 31): family, language, land and nation.

records.source: וּלְשֵׁ֥ם יֻלַּ֖ד גַּם־ה֑וּא אֲבִי֙ כָּל־בְּנֵי־עֵ֔בֶר אֲחִ֖י יֶ֥פֶת הַגָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And to Shem was born, also to him, [the] father of all [the] sons of Eber, [the] brother of Japheth the elder.
pieces: Sons were also born to Shem, the elder brother of Japheth; Shem was the ancestor of all the sons of Eber.

L.21: And to Shem also, the father of all the sons of Eber, the elder brother of Japheth, [sons] were born.

R.21: Shem also had sons. Shem was Japheth's older brother, and he was the ancestor of all the people of Eber.

decisions.choice: the elder brother of Japheth: Shem the elder
alternatives: the brother of Japheth the elder (Japheth the eldest)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean that Shem is Japheth's elder brother, or that Shem is the brother of Japheth, who is the eldest. The order of the list (Shem, Ham, Japheth) and 9:24 (Ham the youngest) do not settle it.

decisions.choice: the sons of Eber: the line that leads to the Hebrews
decisions.reason: Shem is introduced as the ancestor of Eber's line before his sons are named. The name Eber is linked with the word "Hebrew" (14:13); through Eber the line leads to Abraham (11:14-26).

decisions.choice: [sons] were born
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb has no subject; Literal brackets "sons".

records.heading: The descendants of Shem

records.source: בְּנֵ֥י שֵׁ֖ם עֵילָ֣ם וְאַשּׁ֑וּר וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד וְל֥וּד וַֽאֲרָֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram.
pieces: The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram.

L.22: The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram.

R.22: Shem's sons were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram.

decisions.choice: Shem's line: the peoples to the east
decisions.reason: Elam lay east of Babylonia, Asshur is Assyria, and Aram the Arameans of Syria. Arpachshad leads to Eber and Abraham (verse 24; 11:10-26).

records.source: וּבְנֵ֖י אֲרָ֑ם ע֥וּץ וְח֖וּל וְגֶ֥תֶר וָמַֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Aram: Uz and Hul and Gether and Mash.
pieces: The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.

L.23: And the sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.

R.23: Aram's sons were Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.

decisions.choice: Uz: the land of Job
decisions.reason: Uz is the name of the land where Job lived (Job 1:1).

records.source: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד יָלַ֣ד אֶת־שָׁ֑לַח וְשֶׁ֖לַח יָלַ֥ד אֶת־עֵֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: And Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
pieces: Arpachshad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.

L.24: And Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.

R.24: Arpachshad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.

records.source: וּלְעֵ֥בֶר יֻלַּ֖ד שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים שֵׁ֣ם הָֽאֶחָ֞ד פֶּ֗לֶג כִּ֤י בְיָמָיו֙ נִפְלְגָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יָקְטָֽן׃
records.gloss: And to Eber were born two sons; [the] name of the one [was] Peleg, for in his days was divided the earth; and [the] name of his brother [was] Joktan.
pieces: Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.

L.25: And to Eber were born two sons: the name of the one [was] Peleg, for in his days the earth was divided; and the name of his brother [was] Joktan.

R.25: Eber had two sons. One was named Peleg, which means "division," because in his time the people of the earth were divided. His brother was named Joktan.

decisions.choice: Peleg ... was divided: a play on the name
decisions.reason: The name Peleg sounds like the verb "was divided" (niflegah).

decisions.choice: in his days the earth was divided: most likely the scattering at Babel
alternatives: the land was divided by channels or rivers
decisions.reason: "The earth" can mean its people (11:1). The division is most likely the dividing of humankind into peoples and languages at Babel (11:8-9). Others take it as a division of land.

decisions.choice: which means "division"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name so the reason given makes sense (m1).

records.source: וְיָקְטָ֣ן יָלַ֔ד אֶת־אַלְמוֹדָ֖ד וְאֶת־שָׁ֑לֶף וְאֶת־חֲצַרְמָ֖וֶת וְאֶת־יָֽרַח׃
records.gloss: And Joktan fathered Almodad and Sheleph and Hazarmaveth and Jerah,
pieces: Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

L.26: And Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

R.26: Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

decisions.choice: Joktan's sons: peoples of southern Arabia
decisions.reason: The thirteen names of verses 26-29 are tribes of southern Arabia. Hazarmaveth is the region of Hadramaut in Yemen.

records.source: וְאֶת־הֲדוֹרָ֥ם וְאֶת־אוּזָ֖ל וְאֶת־דִּקְלָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Hadoram and Uzal and Diklah,
pieces: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

records.source: וְאֶת־עוֹבָ֥ל וְאֶת־אֲבִֽימָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת־שְׁבָֽא׃
records.gloss: and Obal and Abimael and Sheba,
pieces: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

records.source: וְאֶת־אוֹפִ֥ר וְאֶת־חֲוִילָ֖ה וְאֶת־יוֹבָ֑ב כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י יָקְטָֽן׃
records.gloss: and Ophir and Havilah and Jobab; all these [were the] sons of Joktan.
pieces: Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.

L.29: Ophir, Havilah and Jobab; all these [were] the sons of Joktan.

R.29: Ophir, Havilah and Jobab. All these were Joktan's sons.

decisions.choice: Ophir: the land of gold
decisions.reason: Ophir was famous for its gold, brought by Solomon's ships (1 Kings 9:28). Its location is unknown, perhaps in Arabia.

records.source: וַֽיְהִ֥י מוֹשָׁבָ֖ם מִמֵּשָׁ֑א בֹּאֲכָ֥ה סְפָ֖רָה הַ֥ר הַקֶּֽדֶם׃
records.gloss: And was their dwelling from Mesha as you go toward Sephar, [the] hill country of the east.
pieces: The region where they lived stretched from Mesha toward Sephar, in the eastern hill country.

L.30: And their dwelling was from Mesha in the direction of Sephar, the hill country of the east.

R.30: They lived in the land that reached from Mesha toward Sephar, in the hills to the east.

decisions.choice: from Mesha toward Sephar: places in Arabia, not identified
decisions.reason: Neither place is known for certain; both are in Arabia, "the east" as seen from Israel.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי־שֵׁ֔ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לִלְשֹׁנֹתָ֑ם בְּאַרְצֹתָ֖ם לְגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: These [are the] sons of Shem according to their clans, according to their languages, in their lands, according to their nations.
pieces: These are the descendants of Shem, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.

L.31: These [are] the sons of Shem, by their clans and their languages, in their lands, by their nations.

R.31: These were Shem's descendants. They lived in their own lands, in their own families and nations, each with its own language.

records.source: אֵ֣לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֧ת בְּנֵי־נֹ֛חַ לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶ֑ם וּמֵאֵ֜לֶּה נִפְרְד֧וּ הַגּוֹיִ֛ם בָּאָ֖רֶץ אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃פ
records.gloss: These [are the] clans of [the] sons of Noah according to their generations, in their nations; and from these separated the nations on the earth after the flood.
pieces: These are the clans of Noah's sons, by their family lines, in their nations. From these the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.

L.32: These [are] the clans of the sons of Noah, by their generations, in their nations; and from these the nations spread out on the earth after the flood.

R.32: These are the families of Noah's sons, nation by nation. From them came all the nations that spread out over the earth after the flood.

decisions.choice: the nations spread out on the earth: one human family
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as it began: all nations come from one family. Paul says God "made from one man every nation of humankind to live on all the face of the earth" (Acts 17:26). The next chapter tells how they came to be scattered.
